item.description: - Copy something, dictate, then press ⌘V and you get what you copied, not your dictation a second time. Rhino now puts your clipboard back the moment you paste, without making you wait 5 seconds first. - Long dictated messages are split into a greeting line, paragraphs and a sign-off instead of landing as one block.

- Dictating into text boxes in Chrome, like a GitHub comment box, no longer stops working after the first dictation. Rhino now writes your words to the clipboard right away and puts your previous clipboard back 5 seconds later, so a ⌘V of your own in those 5 seconds pastes the dictation.

- Rhino uses much less memory when you're not dictating. Whisper models now leave memory after 5 idle minutes and reload when you start recording, and the AI cleanup model waits for your first recording instead of loading at launch. - With "Pause media during recording" on, YouTube in Chrome now picks back up after you dictate instead of staying paused. It stays paused, as before, if two tabs were playing, if Music or Spotify was also playing, or if Chrome isn't in English.
